biological.citation: Regulation of cortical neurogenesis by MED13L via transcriptional priming and its implications for MED13L syndrome (PMID: 40775066)
biological.summary: Med13l knockout mice are neonatal lethal with reduced brain volume and cortical thickness. Heterozygotes are viable and show learning/memory deficits, reduced motor coordination, anxiety and microcephaly. Single-cell transcriptomics showed impaired neural progenitor differentiation. MED13L primes transcriptional activation of Neurod2, Sox5, Auts2 and Nfib by binding the core Mediator and facilitating its association with RNA Pol II.

biological.citation: Expression Analyses of Mediator Complex Subunit 13-Like: A Responsible Gene for Neurodevelopmental Disorders during Mouse Brain Development (PMID: 33794529)
biological.summary: MED13L expression is tissue- and developmental stage-dependent in mouse. It is enriched in the ventricular zone and in cytoplasm and nucleus of cortical plate neurons at E14, and becomes diffusely cytoplasmic by P30. It partially colocalizes with synaptophysin and PSD95 in cultured hippocampal neurons, suggesting a role in CNS development and synaptic function.

biological.citation: ASHG 2022 - MED13L knockout in cerebral organoids leads to a shifted developmental program through abnormal cis-regulatory element activation
biological.summary: In MED13L knockout hiPSC-derived cerebral organoids, scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq showed only neuroretinal cells, whereas wild-type organoids produced cortical neurons. Neuroretinal OTX2 and PAX6 cis-regulatory elements were aberrantly activated and forebrain OTX2 CREs (AN1, AN2) were not. Neuroretinal genes such as CRX, VSX and USH2A were upregulated, indicating MED13L is needed for proper enhancer activation during neural induction.

biological.citation: Molecular and Functional Characterisation of a Novel Intragenic 12q24.21 Deletion Resulting in MED13L Haploinsufficiency Syndrome (PMID: 37512036)
biological.summary: CRISPR-Cas9 editing of MED13L in control skin fibroblasts reduced cell viability, accelerated aging, and inhibited expression of RB1, E2F1 and CCNC. The patient's exon 3-10 deletion is predicted to produce a truncated protein lacking the MedPIWI and Med13_C domains.

biological.citation: ASHG 2018 - Functional analysis of MED13L missense variants
biological.summary: MED13L is a CDK8-kinase module subunit of Mediator, paralogous to MED13. Seven de novo missense variants cluster in exons 15-17 and 25-31, predicted to disrupt phosphorylation and ubiquitination sites respectively. FBXW7-dependent ubiquitination assays, phosphorylation assays, localization analysis and zebrafish RNA rescue assays were used to test their consequences.

biological.citation: ASHG 2012 - De novo translocation disrupting Mediator complex subunit in a patient with Pierre-Robin sequence and developmental delay
biological.summary: A de novo t(12;19) translocation disrupting MED13L reduced transcript and protein by more than 50% in patient lymphoblastoid cells. Orthologs are enriched in the brain of zebrafish and in the branchial arches of mouse embryo, and in the hippocampus and dentate gyrus of mouse and human.

biological.citation: Interactions Between Dietary Metabolites and Regulatory Risk Variants for Human Colon Cancer (PMID: 40964363)
biological.summary: An MPRA of 3703 regulatory CRC-associated variants in human colonic cells, treated with butyrate and deoxycholic acid, identified variant-metabolite interactions implicating MED13L, NKD2 and Wnt/β-catenin modulators in CRC gene-environment interactions.

biological.citation: Integrative functional genomics and fine-mapping identify regulatory mechanisms of multivariate obesity GWAS and its cardiometabolic implications (PMID: 41570977)
biological.summary: Multivariate obesity GWAS integrated with adipose chromatin accessibility, eQTL, TWAS/PWAS, fine-mapping and colocalization prioritized MED13L as a key candidate gene. It is among 150 high-confidence genes enriched for neuronal signaling and synaptic organization.

biological.citation: ASHG 2014 - A Novel Mutation, p.(Lys1474*), in a Female adds Seizures and Ptosis to Clinical Findings in MED13L Haploinsufficiency Syndrome
biological.summary: MED13L is a Mediator subunit acting as a transcriptional coactivator for most RNA Pol II genes, and is highly expressed in early heart and brain development. Gene dosage matters: loss-of-function causes haploinsufficiency syndrome, while a 12q24.2 triplication gives a milder phenotype.

biological.citation: MED13L haploinsufficiency syndrome: A de novo frameshift and recurrent intragenic deletions due to parental mosaicism (PMID: 28371282)
biological.summary: A de novo frameshift and an inherited in-frame intragenic deletion of exons 3-14, transmitted from a mosaic mother, were identified in MED13L haploinsufficiency syndrome. One sibling had craniosynostosis, a phenotype not previously reported.
